name: NIST SP 800-171 (Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information)
description: Security requirements for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in non-federal systems. Revision 3 (May 2024) restructured the catalogue to 97 requirements across 17 families, down from 110 in Revision 2, and added three families: Planning (03.15), System and Services Acquisition (03.16) and Supply Chain Risk Management (03.17). A contract citing "800-171" without a revision is ambiguous, and many contracts still specify Rev 2 — confirm the revision per contract, because the requirement counts and family structure differ. Reaches Canadian contractors through defence-adjacent and some nuclear flow-down clauses. One representative requirement per family is catalogued here; the full 97 apply where a contract invokes the standard.
authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
scope: Non-federal organizations processing, storing or transmitting Controlled Unclassified Information under contract
changes_summary: 97 requirements across 17 families (from 110 across 14). Added Planning, System and Services Acquisition, and Supply Chain Risk Management families; withdrew or consolidated requirements judged redundant; introduced organization-defined parameters.

families.name: Access, Identity and Awareness (03.01, 03.02, 03.05)
families.description: Who may reach CUI, how they are authenticated, and whether they know their obligations.

controls.name: Account Management
controls.description: System accounts are managed across their lifecycle and access to CUI is limited to authorized users, processes and devices.

controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.description: Multi-factor authentication is enforced for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts reaching CUI.

controls.name: Literacy Training and Awareness
controls.description: Personnel are made aware of the security risks of their activities and the policies and procedures applying to CUI handling.

families.name: Audit, Configuration and Maintenance (03.03, 03.04, 03.07, 03.08)
families.description: Operational discipline around the systems that hold CUI.

controls.name: Event Logging
controls.description: Audit records are created and retained to enable monitoring, analysis and investigation of unlawful or unauthorized activity.

controls.name: Baseline Configuration
controls.description: Baseline configurations are established and maintained, and systems are configured to the most restrictive mode consistent with operational need.

controls.name: Maintenance Tools
controls.description: Maintenance tools and remote maintenance sessions are controlled, approved, monitored and terminated on completion.

controls.name: Media Sanitization
controls.description: Media containing CUI is sanitized or destroyed before disposal or release for reuse, with the action recorded.

families.name: Protection and Integrity (03.13, 03.14, 03.10)
families.description: Cryptographic and boundary protection, integrity monitoring and physical protection.

controls.name: Transmission and Storage Confidentiality
controls.description: Cryptographic mechanisms protect the confidentiality of CUI in transit and at rest.

controls.name: Boundary Protection
controls.description: Communications at external and key internal boundaries are monitored and controlled, with CUI environments separated from general-purpose networks.

controls.name: Flaw Remediation
controls.description: System flaws are identified, reported and corrected within defined timeframes.

controls.name: Physical Access Authorizations
controls.description: Physical access to systems, equipment and operating environments holding CUI is limited to authorized individuals and logged.

families.name: Risk, Assessment, Incident and Personnel (03.11, 03.12, 03.06, 03.09)
families.description: The management processes that keep the technical requirements honest.

controls.name: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
controls.description: Systems are scanned for vulnerabilities on a defined frequency and when new vulnerabilities affecting the system are identified.

controls.name: Security Assessment
controls.description: Controls are assessed periodically to determine whether they are implemented correctly and producing the intended outcome.

controls.name: Incident Handling
controls.description: An operational incident-handling capability covers preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery and user response, with reporting to the required authorities.

controls.name: Personnel Termination and Transfer
controls.description: Access to CUI is protected during and after personnel actions such as termination and transfer, with credentials revoked and property returned.

families.name: New in Revision 3 (03.15, 03.16, 03.17)
families.description: The three families Revision 3 added. A programme documented against Rev 2 will have no coverage here, which is the specific thing to check when a contract moves to Rev 3.

controls.name: Policy and Procedures (Planning)
controls.description: Policies and procedures for each requirement family are documented, disseminated, reviewed and updated on a defined cycle.

controls.name: Rules of Behavior
controls.description: Rules describing responsibilities and expected behaviour for CUI handling are established and acknowledged by users before access is granted.

controls.name: Security Requirements in Acquisition
controls.description: Security and CUI-protection requirements are included in acquisitions of systems, components and services.

controls.name: Supply Chain Risk Management Plan
controls.description: A plan addresses supply-chain risks to systems and components handling CUI, including subcontractors and the provenance of critical components.
